bar-and-constraints-first.why: The response opens with an explicit constraints table covering latency (p50/p95), context window, streaming, data privacy, minimum quality bar (80%), cost ceiling ($/1K requests), and volume — all defined before any model comparison begins.

eval-driven-not-leaderboard.why: Explicitly warns in a callout box that quality scores are placeholders and instructs the team to run candidates against their own eval set covering continuation coherence, style consistency, and user-acceptance rate, explicitly rejecting reliance on public benchmarks.

quantified-cost-latency.why: Provides specific $/1K request figures for each model, p50 and p95 TTFT values, monthly and annual cost projections at stated volume (100M req/day), and a 10x volume sensitivity row — all quantitative, not vague adjectives.

cheapest-that-clears.why: The matrix and cost tables clearly show cheaper models (Gemini Flash, Haiku) that clear constraints, and GPT-4o is eliminated for cost/latency failures, but the response is cut off before an explicit final recommendation applying this principle is stated.

multiple-candidates.why: Evaluates five candidates spanning frontier (GPT-4o), mid-tier (GPT-4o mini, Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash), and self-hosted open-weight (Llama 3.1 8B), covering API and self-hosted tiers.

sensitivity.why: Includes a 10x volume row showing cost implications but does not explicitly discuss re-evaluation triggers or what quality/price/volume changes would shift the recommendation between models.

lock-in-portability.why: The decision matrix includes an explicit 'Lock-in risk' row rating each model (Medium for OpenAI options, Low for Anthropic/Google, Very Low for self-hosted), directly addressing portability concerns.
